clue.text: Healthy Andrea represented as this?

indicators.note: to represent something is to present it afresh in another form, so the letters before it are set out anew

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone asks how a woman called Andrea, fit and well, should be described.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the letters of the first two words rearrange into a phrase that describes a healthy Andrea.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a fixed idiom for someone robust and in vigorous good health, which is what the clue says Andrea is.

clue.text: A Dalmatian, perhaps, having swallowed a little Bonio, is agile figure

indicators.note: what has been swallowed ends up inside the swallower, so one piece goes within another
only a small portion of the following word is wanted, namely its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
Dalmatia is a region of Croatia, so a Dalmatian is an example of a Croat
first letter of Bonio, a British brand of dog biscuit

explanation.surface: A spotted dog that has eaten a dog biscuit is lively and nimble.
explanation.walkthrough: Dalmatian suggests the dog breed, but it means a person from Dalmatia on the Croatian coast. A + CRO(B)AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus tumbler or gymnast performs feats of balance and nimbleness, an agile performer.

clue.text: Perhaps the PM's hiding fondness, in the end, for EU members

indicators.note: something hidden is tucked away inside, so the first part encloses the next
points to the final letter of the word it is attached to, and nothing else

blocks.note: many British prime ministers went to Eton College, so the PM is an example of an old boy of that school
last letter of fondness

explanation.surface: A prime minister is perhaps concealing a soft spot for the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is an elite English boarding school that has educated many prime ministers. E(S)TONIANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia joined the European Union in 2004, so its citizens are people of a member state.

clue.text: Some leaner vegan sauce

indicators.note: only some of the following words is wanted, a run of letters sitting within them

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A recipe for a lighter dressing suitable for vegans.
explanation.walkthrough: Sauce looks like the culinary noun, but here it is the informal word for impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce is informal British slang for cheek or impudence, and nerve can mean brazen boldness of the same kind.

clue.text: Run not especially serious car part

blocks.note: to head an organisation is to run it
light entertainment is not weighty or serious

explanation.surface: Someone describes a rather casual jog or campaign, then names a component of a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The lamp at the front of a vehicle that lights the road ahead is a component of every car.

clue.text: Storyteller with a stuck-up attitude

indicators.note: in a down entry, something stuck up is turned to read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a pose is an affected attitude or posture

explanation.surface: A narrator who comes across as snobbish and superior.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuck-up reads as snobbish, but it tells you to flip the word for attitude upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek author was famous for his fables, short moral tales such as the tortoise and the hare.

clue.text: Housework restored dignity

indicators.note: something restored has been rebuilt, so the letters of the next word are put back together differently

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Doing chores around the home gave someone back their self-respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting rooms in order and clearing up clutter is a core domestic chore, so the noun fits housework.

clue.text: Oddly superfast fish

indicators.note: keep the letters in odd-numbered positions, the first, third, fifth and so on

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A strangely speedy creature of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A small silvery sea fish of the herring family, often eaten whole or used as bait.

clue.text: Officers have children in very little time

blocks.note: a second is a tiny moment of time
animals that mate breed and produce young

explanation.surface: Officials who start families in no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue in the reverse of the order they take in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: On a merchant ship, the deck officers rank below the master and first in line, so these are ship's officers.

clue.text: Carelessly I drop cash, being delirious

indicators.note: done carelessly, things fall in a jumble, so the letters that follow land in a new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone so overjoyed that they let money fall from their pockets without noticing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rhapsodic means wildly enthusiastic and ecstatic, carried away with joy, which is the sense of delirious here.

clue.text: Aye, cedar was cooked for rye bread ingredient

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the preceding letters are mixed into something new

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that cedar wood was baked to flavour a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The aromatic seeds of an umbelliferous plant give traditional rye loaves their distinctive flavour and are baked into them.

clue.text: Chop up 'n' treat, they say, something made of leather?

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the sound counts and not the spelling

blocks.note: to chop food into small squares is to cube it, and to cure a patient is to heal them

explanation.surface: Instructions to dice some food and serve it as a treat, then a question about leather.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: such shoe parts are often, not always, leather.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban heel is a moderately high, straight-fronted heel on a boot or shoe, commonly built from stacked layers of hide.

clue.text: Top monk, nosey parker reportedly

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so it is the sound of the phrase before it that matters

blocks.note: a nosey parker pries into other people's business

explanation.surface: The head of a monastery is said to be a meddlesome busybody.
explanation.walkthrough: A nosey parker is a British expression for an inquisitive busybody.
explanation.definitionFit: In a religious house the prior ranks just below an abbot, or heads a priory, so is a senior monk.

clue.text: Man compared to Newman a lot

blocks.note: the word Man makes up a part of Newman, so one is set against the other by size
a British slang phrase meaning very much, emphatically

explanation.surface: An ordinary chap is said to measure up poorly against the film star Paul Newman.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is exactly half of Newman, so the phrase is used with a wink; as slang, the expression means the opposite of its literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In British speech the phrase is an emphatic yes, meaning extremely or very much, as in 'did you enjoy it? Not half!'

clue.text: In a flap, freed hens perked up

indicators.note: being in a flap means flustered and agitated, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Chickens released from their coop flutter about, livelier than before.
explanation.definitionFit: To be refreshed or revived is to be given new energy, as when someone brightens and becomes livelier.

clue.text: A song, Hollow Aura Surrounding City

indicators.note: something hollow has had its middle scooped out, leaving only the outside letters of the preceding word
the word before goes round the material in front of it, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written
first and last letters of song
a glow is a radiance or aura around something

explanation.surface: A title in capitals, as if for an empty-sounding tune about an aura around a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasgow is the largest city in Scotland, on the River Clyde.

clue.text: A lake in European country – or one far away

indicators.note: the first two pieces are placed inside the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the standard map abbreviation for lake
a land-locked country in central Europe

explanation.surface: A lake set in an Alpine nation, contrasted with a distant country.
explanation.walkthrough: One far away is a country too, picking up 'country' from earlier in the clue. AUSTR(A L)IA.
explanation.definitionFit: The southern hemisphere continent-nation lies on the opposite side of the globe from Europe, about as distant as a land can be.

clue.text: Trapped in laundromat is sensitive artist

indicators.note: something trapped in the following words is caught inside them as a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: the run spanning the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A touchy painter is stuck inside a self-service launderette.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, a leader of the Fauvist movement known for bold colour and paper cut-outs.

explanation.surface: Three grand visitors from the East arrive bearing myrrh and gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word after the indicator contributes its first letter, while the whole clue also describes the answer.

clue.text: Cuts damaged a big city somewhere in Italy

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder
taken as written
NY is the abbreviation for New York, the big city

explanation.surface: Spending cuts have harmed a major city in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscany is a region of central Italy whose capital is Florence, so it is a place within the country.

clue.text: Once more, holy man is contrary

blocks.note: again means one more time
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A saintly figure is being awkward yet again.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed or in opposition to something is to be contrary to it, as in 'against the rules'.

clue.text: Tusk's one with power

definitions.note: a tusk is one of these, so the plural is defined by an example of a single member

blocks.note: first meaning: a tusk is one of an animal's long protruding dental growths
second meaning: effective force, as a law that has real bite

explanation.surface: An elephant's ivory is described as something with strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A tusk is a very long tooth, and figuratively a rule with real enforcement force is said to have these.

clue.text: Criticised drunken topless fathead trashing Spain

indicators.note: without a top, the word loses its first letter
trashing something throws it away, so that letter is discarded
a drunk staggers about in disorder, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A drunk, bare-chested idiot was told off for wrecking things in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove F from the front and E from inside FATHEAD, leaving ATHAD to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To have at someone is an old idiom for attacking them, physically or with words, so the past tense means laid into.

clue.text: Two thirds of Irish had a meal and sleep

indicators.note: only two thirds of the next word is kept, so its final third is dropped

blocks.note: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland, so its adjective means Irish
to eat a meal

explanation.surface: Someone from Ireland has dinner and then goes to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine-letter Latinate word loses its last three letters, keeping six.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that hibernate pass the winter in a deep dormant state, a long seasonal sleep.

clue.text: Big vehicle, tyre's not about to be pneumatic

indicators.note: not tells you to leave out the next word's letters from the one before

blocks.note: a bus is a large road vehicle
taken as written
re is Latin for about, concerning

explanation.surface: A large vehicle whose tyre is about to be inflated with air.
explanation.walkthrough: Pneumatic looks like air-filled tyres, but it is old slang for a woman with a full figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Pneumatic is jocular, slightly dated slang for a curvaceous woman with an ample bosom, the same sense as the answer.

clue.text: Maniac Musk lands dramatic wins

indicators.note: a maniac behaves wildly, so the letters that follow are thrown into a crazy new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: The eccentric billionaire Elon Musk secures some spectacular victories.

clue.text: A warm jacket may be so worn

definitions.text: A warm jacket may be so

blocks.clueFragment: A warm jacket may be so
blocks.note: first meaning: having an inner layer of fabric sewn inside
second meaning: creased with wrinkles, as an aged face

explanation.walkthrough: Worn seems to describe the jacket being worn, but it stands alone as a description of a tired, wrinkled face.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat with padding inside is said to have this quality, and a careworn face marked with wrinkles is also described so.

clue.text: The present time?

blocks.note: surface reading: now, the current moment
setter's reading: an occasion for giving gifts

explanation.walkthrough: Present looks like the opposite of past, but it means a gift, and the time is the celebration when gifts are handed over.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual celebration of someone's birth is the occasion when guests traditionally bring gifts for the honoured person.
